docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:56:**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:62:**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:70:**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.

Non-limit exit → retry once then park (attempt-driven), no bundle transitions. Model-unavailable at spawn → dead {platform, model} added to avoidEntries, re-resolve to the SAME platform's next entry, relaunch, no seal/receive. Usage-limit → the ordered transaction on the REAL command machinery: loop position checkpointed into the bundle under the supervisor session BEFORE the seal; finalize with reasonClass usage-limit (degraded-open path also pinned); receive prepare+commit back-to-back with identical flags/session; zero .handoff/loop writes across the transaction (fs spy); injected window drift → one automatic re-prepare retry; second consecutive stale → park; relaunch assignment avoids the dead origin platform; total exhaustion → park with the classifier's resumeAt hint; deterministic from injected io. reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:4558:docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6325:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:348:    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6696:reviews/2026-07-12-gate-2-final/reviewer-a/iteration-05/raw-output.txt:182:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

It has **no usage-limit handling** — our failover logic is net-new.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7381:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1469:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7495:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:1197:   320	    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7496:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:1225:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7715:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:19077:   808	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

    29	/**
    30	 * Assemble the spawn contract for a role child. Reviewers are read-only on
    31	 * every platform; every child is marked supervised (its own baton hooks
    32	 * no-op), carries the sole-author git identity, and has stdin CLOSED at
    33	 * spawn (the codex-exec stdin-hang field failure).
    34	 * @param {{platform: string, role: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string}} assignment
    35	 * @param {string} prompt
    36	 * @param {{root: string}} opts
    37	 * @returns {{command: string, args: string[], env: Record<string, string>, stdio: any[], cwd: string}}
    38	 */
    39	export function buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, opts) {
    40	  const readOnly = REVIEWER_ROLES.has(assignment.role);
    41	  const env = { BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD: '1', ...GIT_IDENTITY };
    42	  const stdio = ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'];

    44	  if (assignment.platform === 'claude-code') {
    45	    // --model honors the role matrix (and entry-level avoidance);
    46	    // --output-format json is what parseVerdict's claude branch reads; the
    47	    // cwd puts the child in its seat, never the supervisor cwd.
    48	    const args = ['-p', prompt, '--model', assignment.model, '--output-format', 'json'];
    49	    if (readOnly) {
    50	      // Scoped read-only git so a reviewer can actually SEE the diff it

    53	    } else {

    55	    }

    66	const VERDICT_RE = /VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|APPROVED|BLOCKED)\b/g;
    67	
    68	/** @param {string} region @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string} | null} */
    69	function lastVerdictIn(region) {
    70	  let last = null;
    71	  for (const m of region.matchAll(VERDICT_RE)) last = m;
    72	  if (!last) return null;
    73	  const after = region.slice((last.index ?? 0) + last[0].length);
    74	  return { verdict: last[1], findings: after.trim() };
    75	}

    77	/**
    78	 * Region-bounded verdict parsing — the prompt region (which quotes the
    79	 * verdict format in its instructions) is NEVER scanned, and there is no
    80	 * whole-transcript fallback. Unparseable is BLOCKED, never APPROVED.
    81	 * - codex: only the text after the LAST line starting with 'tokens used'.
    82	 * - claude-code: only the `result` field of the structured JSON output.
    83	 * Multiple tails inside the trusted region → the LAST one wins.
    84	 * @param {string} transcript @param {{platform: string}} opts
    85	 * @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string, reason?: string}}
    86	 */
    87	export function parseVerdict(transcript, { platform }) {
    88	  const unparseable = { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: '', reason: 'unparseable' };
    89	  const text = String(transcript ?? '');
    90	
    91	  if (platform === 'claude-code') {
    92	    let obj = null;
    93	    try {
    94	      obj = JSON.parse(text.trim());
    95	    } catch {
    96	      return unparseable;
    97	    }
    98	    if (typeof obj?.result !== 'string') return unparseable;
    99	    const hit = lastVerdictIn(obj.result);
   100	    return hit ?? unparseable;
   101	  }
   102	
   103	  // codex: locate the LAST 'tokens used' marker line; the trusted region is
   104	  // strictly after it.
   105	  const lines = text.split('\n');
   106	  let markerLine = -1;
   107	  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
   108	    if (/^tokens used\b/i.test(lines[i])) markerLine = i;
   109	  }
   110	  if (markerLine === -1) return unparseable;
   111	  const region = lines.slice(markerLine + 1).join('\n');
   112	  const hit = lastVerdictIn(region);
   113	  return hit ?? unparseable;
   114	}
   115	
   116	const TRUNCATION_MARKER = '\n[... truncated by baton log cap ...]\n';
   117	
   118	/**
   119	 * Cap a transcript: head preserved, middle replaced with a marker, TAIL
   120	 * preserved verbatim (the verdict lives at the end and must never be cut).
   121	 * @param {string} text @param {number} maxBytes
   122	 * @returns {string}
   123	 */
   124	export function capLog(text, maxBytes) {
   125	  const s = String(text ?? '');
   126	  if (Buffer.byteLength(s) <= maxBytes) return s;
   127	  const headBytes = Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxBytes * 0.4));
   128	  const tailBytes = Math.max(1, maxBytes - headBytes);
   129	  const buf = Buffer.from(s);
   130	  const head = buf.subarray(0, headBytes).toString();
   131	  const tail = buf.subarray(buf.length - tailBytes).toString();
   132	  return head + TRUNCATION_MARKER + tail;
   133	}

   139	 * @returns {string}

   141	export function classifyChildExit(transcript, exitCode, platform, table) {
   142	  return classify({ text: transcript, exitCode, platform, table }).class;

   146	function killGroup(pid, sig) {

   148	    process.kill(-pid, sig);

   150	    // ESRCH — already gone.

   154	/**
   155	 * Spawn and supervise one child: detached in its OWN process group, stdin
   156	 * closed; on timeout SIGTERM the group, wait graceMs, SIGKILL the group (no
   157	 * zombie grandchildren). Output streams to a capped log at opts.logPath; the
   158	 * verdict is parsed from the full transcript, region-bounded.
   159	 * @param {{command: string, args: string[], env?: Record<string, string>, cwd?: string}} spec
   160	 * @param {{timeoutMs: number, graceMs: number, logPath: string, maxLogBytes?: number, platform?: string, onStart?: (info: {pid: number, pgid: number}) => void}} opts
   161	 * @returns {Promise<{timedOut: boolean, exitCode: number | null, verdict?: string, findings?: string, reason?: string, logPath: string, pgid?: number}>}
   162	 */
   163	export function superviseChild(spec, opts) {
   164	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
   165	    const maxLogBytes = opts.maxLogBytes ?? 1_000_000;
   166	    const child = spawn(spec.command, spec.args, {
   167	      cwd: spec.cwd,
   168	      env: { ...process.env, ...(spec.env ?? {}) },
   169	      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
   170	      detached: true, // its own process group — the kill unit
   171	    });
   172	
   173	    // Report the group at spawn time so the supervisor can persist it BEFORE
   174	    // the child completes — a supervisor crash leaves the orphan reap-able.
   175	    const pgid = typeof child.pid === 'number' ? child.pid : -1;
   176	    if (typeof opts.onStart === 'function' && typeof child.pid === 'number') {
   177	      opts.onStart({ pid: child.pid, pgid });
   178	    }
   179	
   180	    let out = '';
   181	    let timedOut = false;
   182	    /** @type {NodeJS.Timeout | null} */
   183	    let killTimer = null;
   184	
   185	    const onChunk = (/** @type {Buffer} */ c) => {
   186	      out += c.toString();
   187	    };
   188	    child.stdout?.on('data', onChunk);
   189	    child.stderr?.on('data', onChunk);
   190	
   191	    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
   192	      timedOut = true;
   193	      if (typeof child.pid === 'number') {
   194	        killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
   195	        killTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   196	          if (typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   197	        }, opts.graceMs);
   198	      }
   199	    }, opts.timeoutMs);
   200	
   201	    const finish = (/** @type {number | null} */ exitCode) => {
   202	      clearTimeout(timeout);
   203	      if (killTimer) clearTimeout(killTimer);
   204	      // Belt-and-braces: reap any group survivors even on a clean exit path.
   205	      if (timedOut && typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   206	      try {
   207	        mkdirSync(dirname(opts.logPath), { recursive: true });
   208	        writeFileSync(opts.logPath, capLog(out, maxLogBytes));
   209	      } catch {
   210	        // The log must never mask the result.
   211	      }
   212	      const parsed = parseVerdict(out, { platform: opts.platform ?? 'codex' });
   213	      resolve({
   214	        timedOut,
   215	        exitCode: timedOut ? null : exitCode,
   216	        verdict: parsed.verdict,
   217	        findings: parsed.findings,
   218	        ...(parsed.reason ? { reason: parsed.reason } : {}),
   219	        logPath: opts.logPath,
   220	        pgid,
   221	      });
   222	    };
   223	
   224	    child.on('error', () => finish(null));
   225	    child.on('close', (code) => finish(code));
   226	  });
   227	}

    90	/**
    91	 * Preflight before a child runs in a seat: the worktree is listed, its index
    92	 * is clean, and HEAD sits on the expected branch. Refusals name the failed
    93	 * check and never issue destructive git.
    94	 * @param {string} root @param {{seat: string, branch: string}} target @param {any} io
    95	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true} | {ok: false, check: string, refusal: string}>}

    97	export async function preflightWorktree(root, target, io) {
    98	  const path = worktreePaths(root).seats[target.seat];
    99	  const listed = parseWorktreeList((await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).stdout);
   100	  if (!listed.some((e) => e.path === path)) {
   101	    return { ok: false, check: 'missing-worktree', refusal: `worktree ${path} is not listed by git — run setup or self-heal first` };

   120	export async function postflightWorktree(root, target, io) {

   122	  const head = (await git(io, path, ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'])).stdout.trim();
   123	  if (head !== target.branch) {

   133	/**
   134	 * Full-range attribution scan over main..branch — the merge gate. Every
   135	 * commit must be authored AND committed by the sole author, with no forbidden
   136	 * AI-attribution trailer in the body. The range is never windowed.
   137	 * @param {string} root @param {string} branch @param {any} io
   138	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true} | {ok: false, offending: string, reason: string}>}
   139	 */
   140	export async function attributionScan(root, branch, io) {
   141	  const out = (await git(io, root, ['log', `main..${branch}`, `--format=${LOG_FORMAT}`])).stdout;
   142	  for (const record of String(out).split('\x1e')) {
   143	    if (record.trim().length === 0) continue;
   144	    const [sha, an, ae, cn, ce, body = ''] = record.replace(/^\n/, '').split('\x00');
   145	    if (an !== SOLE_AUTHOR.name || ae !== SOLE_AUTHOR.email) {
   146	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} has a foreign author identity (${an} <${ae}>) — sole-author is required` };
   147	    }
   148	    if (cn !== SOLE_AUTHOR.name || ce !== SOLE_AUTHOR.email) {
   149	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} has a foreign committer identity (${cn} <${ce}>) — sole-author is required` };
   150	    }
   151	    if (TRAILER_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(body))) {
   152	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} carries a forbidden AI-attribution trailer (co-authored/generated-with/emoji) in its message` };
   153	    }
   154	  }
   155	  return { ok: true };
   156	}

   158	const mergeLockPath = (/** @type {string} */ root) => `${root}/.handoff/loop/merge.lock`;
   159	
   160	/**
   161	 * Merge an approved subtask branch into main — one guarded transaction:
   162	 * acquire the merge lock (a held lock refuses), gate on the attribution scan,
   163	 * merge at the repo root, abort-and-park on conflict, then ff-only sync both
   164	 * seats. The lock is released on EVERY exit path after acquisition.
   165	 * @param {string} root @param {{branch: string}} input @param {any} io
   166	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true, branch: string} | {ok: false, reason: string}>}
   167	 */
   168	export async function mergeSubtask(root, input, io) {
   169	  const lock = mergeLockPath(root);
   170	  if (io.fs.existsSync(lock)) {
   171	    return { ok: false, reason: `the merge lock at ${lock} is held by another merger — refusing a concurrent merge` };
   172	  }
   173	  ensureDir(io.fs, `${root}/.handoff/loop`);
   174	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, lock, { host: io.host, pid: io.pid, at: io.now() });
   175	  try {
   176	    const scan = await attributionScan(root, input.branch, io);
   177	    if (scan.ok !== true) return { ok: false, reason: scan.reason };
   178	
   179	    try {
   180	      await git(io, root, ['merge', input.branch]);
   181	    } catch (err) {
   182	      // Conflict (or any merge failure): abort, never auto-resolve — park.
   183	      try {
   184	        await git(io, root, ['merge', '--abort']);
   185	      } catch {
   186	        // Nothing to abort — the failure predates a merge state.
   187	      }
   188	      const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.stdout || /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message || String(err);
   189	      return { ok: false, reason: `merge conflict — aborted and parked for the operator: ${String(msg).split('\n')[0]}` };
   190	    }
   191	
   192	    const seats = worktreePaths(root).seats;
   193	    for (const seat of SEATS) {
   194	      try {
   195	        await git(io, seats[seat], ['merge', '--ff-only', 'main']);
   196	      } catch (err) {
   197	        const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.stderr || /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message || String(err);
   198	        return { ok: false, reason: `worktree wt-${seat} could not fast-forward to main — corruption signal, parked: ${String(msg).split('\n')[0]}` };
   199	      }
   200	    }
   201	    return { ok: true, branch: input.branch };
   202	  } finally {
   203	    try {
   204	      if (io.fs.existsSync(lock)) io.fs.unlinkSync(lock);
   205	    } catch {
   206	      // Best effort — a leaked lock is visible and operator-recoverable.
   207	    }
   208	  }
   209	}

   234	export async function teardownWorktrees(root, io) {
   235	  const p = worktreePaths(root);
   236	  const listed = parseWorktreeList((await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).stdout);
   237	  /** @type {string[]} */
   238	  const removed = [];

   244	    // that moved on to subtask branches orphans its base otherwise

   257	      }
   258	    }

   260	  }
   261	  return { ok: true, removed };

    41	/**
    42	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    43	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    44	 */
    45	export async function cmdPipeline(args, io) {
    46	  /** @type {string[]} */
    47	  const positionals = [];
    48	  /** @type {string[]} */
    49	  const flagTokens = [];
    50	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    51	    const a = args[i];
    52	    if (typeof a === 'string' && a.startsWith('--')) {
    53	      flagTokens.push(a);
    54	      if (STRING_FLAGS.has(a.slice(2)) && i + 1 < args.length) {
    55	        i += 1;
    56	        flagTokens.push(args[i]);
    57	      }
    58	    } else {
    59	      positionals.push(a);
    60	    }
    61	  }
    62	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(flagTokens, {});
    63	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'pipeline', parsed.error);
    64	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    65	
    66	  const sub = positionals[0];
    67	  if (sub === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', 'a subcommand is required — try: baton pipeline run');
    68	  if (sub !== 'run') return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `unknown subcommand '${sub}' (supported: run)`);
    69	  if (positionals.length > 1) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `unexpected argument '${positionals[1]}'`);
    70	
    71	  return runPipeline(flags, io);
    72	}

    74	/** Validate the spec's subtasks — every rejection names its offender.
    75	 * @param {any} subtasks @returns {string | null} */
    76	function validateSubtasks(subtasks) {
    77	  if (!Array.isArray(subtasks) || subtasks.length === 0) {
    78	    return 'loop.json needs a non-empty `subtasks` array ([{id, title}]) for a pipeline run';
    79	  }
    80	  const seen = new Set();
    81	  for (let i = 0; i < subtasks.length; i += 1) {
    82	    const st = subtasks[i];
    83	    if (typeof st?.id !== 'string' || st.id.length === 0) return `subtasks[${i}] is missing a string id`;
    84	    if (typeof st?.title !== 'string' || st.title.length === 0) return `subtasks[${i}] ('${st.id}') is missing a string title`;
    85	    if (seen.has(st.id)) return `subtasks carry a duplicate id '${st.id}' — ids name branches and must be unique`;
    86	    seen.add(st.id);
    87	  }
    88	  return null;
    89	}

    91	/**
    92	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags @param {any} io
    93	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    94	 */
    95	async function runPipeline(flags, io) {
    96	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    97	  const p = loopPaths(root);
    98	
    99	  const rawSpec = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${root}/loop.json`);
   100	  if (!rawSpec.ok) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `no loop.json at ${root} — scaffold one with: baton loop init "<goal>"`);
   101	  const spec = rawSpec.value;
   102	  const subtaskError = validateSubtasks(spec?.subtasks);
   103	  if (subtaskError !== null) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', subtaskError);
   104	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   105	  if (!config) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `no readable baton.config.json at ${root} — the role matrix is required`);
   106	  // The 5-iteration cap is a hard invariant (Gate-2 fold G2): a spec asking
   107	  // for more is rejected BEFORE anything spawns.
   108	  const rawCap = spec?.budgets?.iterationCap;
   109	  if (rawCap !== undefined && (typeof rawCap !== 'number' || rawCap < 1 || rawCap > 5)) {
   110	    return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `budgets.iterationCap must be a number between 1 and 5 (the 5-iteration cap is a hard invariant; got ${JSON.stringify(rawCap)})`);
   111	  }
   112	  const cap = typeof rawCap === 'number' ? rawCap : 5;
   113	  const timeoutMs = (typeof spec?.budgets?.perRoleTimeoutMin === 'number' ? spec.budgets.perRoleTimeoutMin : 30) * 60_000;
   114	
   115	  // One supervisor at a time — the same atomic run lock as `loop run`, with
   116	  // dead-owner reclaim + orphan reaping (Gate-2 fold G2/B8).
   117	  const lock = await acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, 'pipeline run');
   118	  if (lock.ok !== true) return lock.code;
   119	  try {
   120	    return await drivePipeline(flags, io, { root, p, spec, config, cap, timeoutMs });
   121	  } finally {
   122	    lock.release();
   123	  }
   124	}

   126	/**
   127	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags @param {any} io
   128	 * @param {{root: string, p: any, spec: any, config: any, cap: number, timeoutMs: number}} ctx
   129	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   130	 */
   131	async function drivePipeline(flags, io, { root, p, spec, config, cap, timeoutMs }) {
   132	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
   133	  /** @param {string} role @returns {any | null} */
   134	  const resolveOne = (role) => {
   135	    const a = resolveRoles({ config, to: 'claude-code', avoid: [], avoidEntries: [], probes: null }).assignments[role];
   136	    return a && a.mode !== 'unavailable' ? a : null;
   137	  };
   138	
   139	  // The synthesized phase list makes the loop state machine (phase count,
   140	  // done detection, journal replay) work unchanged for the subtask cycle.
   141	  const subtasks = spec.subtasks;
   142	  const stateSpec = {
   143	    goal: spec.goal,
   144	    phases: subtasks.map((/** @type {any} */ st, /** @type {number} */ i) => ({ id: `subtask-${st.id}`, role: `worker-${i % 2 === 0 ? 'a' : 'b'}` })),
   145	  };
   146	  // RESUME, never re-init: a prior run's cap counters and position survive a
   147	  // re-invocation (Gate-2 fold G2 — no cap refunds).
   148	  /** @type {any} */
   149	  let state = (await loadLoopState(root, io)).state;
   150	  if (state === null) {
   151	    state = initLoopState(stateSpec, io);
   152	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   153	  }
   154	  if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   155	    io.stderr.write(`baton pipeline run: the run is escalated (gate ${state.escalation?.gate}) — see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md\n`);
   156	    return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   157	  }
   158	  if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) {
   159	    io.stderr.write(`baton pipeline run: the run is parked — ${state.parkReason ?? 'no reason recorded'}\n`);
   160	    return EXIT_PARKED;
   161	  }
   162	  const runner = io.superviseChild ?? superviseChild;
   163	  const seats = worktreePaths(root).seats;
   164	  let childSeq = 0;
   165	
   166	  const transition = async (/** @type {any} */ ev) => {
   167	    const next = applyLoopEvent(state, ev);
   168	    const seq = await appendLoopEvent(root, ev, io);
   169	    state = { ...next, journalSeq: seq };
   170	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   171	    return state;
   172	  };
   173	  const park = async (/** @type {string} */ reason) => {
   174	    await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason });
   175	    io.stderr.write(`baton pipeline run: parked — ${reason}\n`);
   176	    return EXIT_PARKED;
   177	  };
   178	
   179	  await setupWorktrees(root, io);
   180	
   181	  const spawn = async (/** @type {any} */ assignment, /** @type {string} */ prompt, /** @type {string} */ seatPath, /** @type {string} */ label) => {
   182	    childSeq += 1;
   183	    const childId = `${String(childSeq).padStart(3, '0')}-${label}`;
   184	    const logPath = `${p.dir}/children/${childId}.log`;
   185	    ensureDir(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children`);
   186	    const childSpec = buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, { root: seatPath });
   187	    return runner(childSpec, {
   188	      timeoutMs,
   189	      graceMs: 10_000,
   190	      logPath,
   191	      maxLogBytes: 1_000_000,
   192	      platform: assignment.platform,
   193	      onStart: (/** @type {{pid: number, pgid: number}} */ info) => {
   194	        appendEntry(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`, { childId, pid: info.pid, pgid: info.pgid, startedAt: io.now() });
   195	      },
   196	    });
   197	  };
   198	
   199	  // Prepare a seat for use, healing a listed-but-raw-deleted worktree (prune
   200	  // + re-add) once before giving up (Gate-2 fold G5).
   201	  const withSeatHealing = async (/** @type {string} */ seat, /** @type {() => Promise<any>} */ fn) => {
   202	    try {
   203	      return await fn();
   204	    } catch (err) {
   205	      const msg = String(/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? err);
   206	      if (/already exists/i.test(msg)) throw err; // a stale branch is a park, not a heal
   207	      await selfHealWorktree(root, { seat, branch: `baton/wt-${seat}/base` }, io);
   208	      return fn();
   209	    }
   210	  };
   211	
   212	  for (let i = state.phaseIndex; i < subtasks.length; i += 1) {
   213	    const st = subtasks[i];
   214	    const seat = i % 2 === 0 ? 'a' : 'b';
   215	    const other = seat === 'a' ? 'b' : 'a';
   216	    const branch = `baton/wt-${seat}/subtask-${st.id}`;
   217	    const gate = `subtask-${st.id}-review`;
   218	
   219	    const writerAssignment = resolveOne(`worker-${seat}`);
   220	    const reviewerModel = resolveOne(`worker-${other}`);
   221	    const mergerModel = resolveOne('merger');
   222	    if (!writerAssignment || !reviewerModel || !mergerModel) {
   223	      return park(`no eligible assignment for subtask '${st.id}' (worker-${seat}/worker-${other}/merger must all resolve)`);
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    // Start the subtask branch in the writer's seat (self-healing a raw-deleted
   227	    // seat), then verify the seat. A pre-existing (stale) branch parks.
   228	    let mainSha;
   229	    try {
   230	      const alreadyOnBranch =
   231	        String((await withSeatHealing(seat, () => io.execFile('git', ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'], { cwd: seats[seat] }))).stdout).trim() === branch;
   232	      if (!alreadyOnBranch) await withSeatHealing(seat, () => io.execFile('git', ['checkout', '-b', branch], { cwd: seats[seat] }));
   233	      const pre = await preflightWorktree(root, { seat, branch }, io);
   234	      if (pre.ok !== true) return park(`preflight refused subtask '${st.id}': ${pre.refusal}`);
   235	      mainSha = (await io.execFile('git', ['rev-parse', 'main'], { cwd: root })).stdout.trim();
   236	    } catch (err) {
   237	      return park(`seat preparation failed for subtask '${st.id}': ${String(/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? err).split('\n')[0]}`);
   238	    }
   239	
   240	    let findings = '';
   241	    let merged = false;
   242	    let failoverAttempt = 0;
   243	    /** @type {any | null} */
   244	    let forcedWriter = null;
   245	    while (!merged) {
   246	      if ((state.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   247	        await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   248	        atomicWriteText(
   249	          io.fs,
   250	          `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`,
   251	          `# Pipeline escalation\n\nGate '${gate}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`,
   252	        );
   253	        io.stderr.write(`baton pipeline run: gate '${gate}' hit the ${cap}-iteration cap — escalated (see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md)\n`);
   254	        return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   255	      }
   256	
   257	      // Writer (write-capable, its own seat).
   258	      const writerAsg = forcedWriter ?? { ...writerAssignment, role: `worker-${seat}` };
   259	      forcedWriter = null;
   260	      const writerPrompt = [
   261	        `You are the writer (worker-${seat}) for subtask '${st.id}': ${st.title}.`,
   262	        `Goal: ${spec.goal}. Work ONLY on branch ${branch} in your worktree; commit your work there.`,
   263	        findings ? `The previous attempt was BLOCKED — address every finding:\n${findings}` : '',
   264	      ]
   265	        .filter(Boolean)
   266	        .join('\n\n');
   267	      const writerResult = await spawn(writerAsg, writerPrompt, seats[seat], `${st.id}-writer`);
   268	
   269	      // The writer's result is CONSUMED, never discarded (Gate-2 fold G3):
   270	      // classify its log first — a limit/model death routes through failover,
   271	      // a BLOCKED self-check retries the writer, and only a passing writer
   272	      // hands off to review.
   273	      const writerLog = writerResult.logPath && io.fs.existsSync(writerResult.logPath) ? io.fs.readFileSync(writerResult.logPath, 'utf8') : '';
   274	      const writerCls = classify({ text: writerLog, exitCode: writerResult.exitCode ?? 0, platform: writerAsg.platform, table }).class;
   275	      if (writerCls !== 'ok') {
   276	        failoverAttempt += 1;
   277	        const decision = await runFailover({
   278	          root,
   279	          io,
   280	          config,
   281	          role: writerAsg.role === 'merger' ? writerAsg.role : `worker-${seat}`,
   282	          assignment: writerAsg,
   283	          transcript: writerLog,
   284	          exitCode: writerResult.exitCode ?? 1,
   285	          sessionHint: `loop-${state.runId}`,
   286	          probes: null,
   287	          avoid: [],
   288	          avoidEntries: [],
   289	          attempt: failoverAttempt,
   290	          loopState: { runId: state.runId, phaseIndex: state.phaseIndex, iterations: state.iterations, status: state.status },
   291	        });
   292	        if (decision.action === 'park') return park(`writer failover parked subtask '${st.id}': ${decision.reason}`);
   293	        if (decision.action === 'relaunch') {
   294	          forcedWriter = { ...decision.assignment, role: `worker-${seat}` };
   295	        }
   296	        continue; // relaunch or retry the writer — never review a failed attempt
   297	      }
   298	      if (writerResult.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && writerResult.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   299	        findings = String(writerResult.findings ?? '');
   300	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   301	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   302	          atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`, `# Pipeline escalation\n\nGate '${gate}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`);
   303	          return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   304	        }
   305	        continue; // the writer retries; no reviewer sees a failed attempt
   306	      }
   307	
   308	      const post = await postflightWorktree(root, { seat, branch, mainSha }, io);
   309	      if (post.ok !== true) return park(`postflight refused subtask '${st.id}': ${post.refusal}`);
   310	
   311	      // An empty branch never merges (Gate-2 fold G3): the writer must have
   312	      // actually committed work ahead of main.
   313	      const ahead = String((await io.execFile('git', ['log', `main..${branch}`, '--format=%H'], { cwd: root })).stdout).trim();
   314	      if (ahead.length === 0) return park(`subtask '${st.id}' produced an EMPTY branch (no commits ahead of main) — nothing to review or merge`);
   315	
   316	      // Reviewer-seat preflight (Gate-2 fold G5): the reviewing seat must be
   317	      // listed and clean before a reviewer spawns into it.
   318	      try {
   319	        const otherBranch = String((await withSeatHealing(other, () => io.execFile('git', ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'], { cwd: seats[other] }))).stdout).trim();
   320	        const reviewerPre = await preflightWorktree(root, { seat: other, branch: otherBranch }, io);
   321	        if (reviewerPre.ok !== true) return park(`reviewer-seat preflight refused subtask '${st.id}': ${reviewerPre.refusal}`);
   322	      } catch (err) {
   323	        return park(`reviewer-seat preparation failed for subtask '${st.id}': ${String(/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? err).split('\n')[0]}`);
   324	      }
   325	
   326	      // Reviewer (read-only, the OTHER seat's model and cwd, subtask-reviewer role).
   327	      const reviewPrompt = [
   328	        `You are the subtask-reviewer for subtask '${st.id}': ${st.title}.`,
   329	        `Review the change on ${branch} against main from the ${other} seat (fresh context). Run: git diff main..${branch} (and git log main..${branch}) to see exactly what changed — branch refs are shared across worktrees.`,
   330	        "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   331	      ].join('\n\n');
   332	      const review = await spawn({ ...reviewerModel, role: 'subtask-reviewer' }, reviewPrompt, seats[other], `${st.id}-review`);
   333	      if (review.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && review.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   334	        findings = String(review.findings ?? '');
   335	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   336	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   337	          atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`, `# Pipeline escalation\n\nGate '${gate}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`);
   338	          return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   339	        }
   340	        continue;
   341	      }
   342	
   343	      // Merger (read-only child — it re-checks; the SUPERVISOR merges).
   344	      const mergerPrompt = [
   345	        `You are the merger for subtask '${st.id}'. Adversarially re-check ${branch} against main before it merges.`,
   346	        "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   347	      ].join('\n\n');
   348	      const mergerVerdict = await spawn({ ...mergerModel, role: 'merger' }, mergerPrompt, root, `${st.id}-merge-check`);
   349	      if (mergerVerdict.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && mergerVerdict.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   350	        findings = String(mergerVerdict.findings ?? '');
   351	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   352	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   353	          atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`, `# Pipeline escalation\n\nGate '${gate}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`);
   354	          return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   355	        }
   356	        continue;
   357	      }
   358	
   359	      const merge = await mergeSubtask(root, { branch }, io);
   360	      if (merge.ok !== true) return park(`merge of '${branch}' refused: ${merge.reason}`);
   361	      merged = true;
   362	    }
   363	
   364	    await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE });
   365	  }
   366	
   367	  if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { status: state.status, subtasks: subtasks.length } });
   368	  else io.stdout.write(`baton pipeline run: done — ${subtasks.length} subtask(s) merged\n`);
   369	  return state.status === LOOP_STATUS.DONE ? 0 : state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED ? EXIT_PARKED : 0;
   370	}

    35	/**
    36	 * `baton loop <subcommand>` — the Layer-2 goal-loop surface. v1 subcommands:
    37	 * `init "<goal>"` (scaffold loop.json; two-phase, idempotent, dry-run-able).
    38	 * Supervisor-side by design: the BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD guard deliberately
    39	 * does NOT apply here.
