    41	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    42	 */
    43	export async function cmdLoop(args, io) {
    44	  /** @type {string[]} */
    45	  const positionals = [];
    46	  /** @type {string[]} */
    47	  const flagTokens = [];
    48	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    49	    const a = args[i];
    50	    if (typeof a === 'string' && a.startsWith('--')) {
    51	      flagTokens.push(a);
    52	      if (STRING_FLAGS.has(a.slice(2)) && i + 1 < args.length) {
    53	        i += 1;
    54	        flagTokens.push(args[i]);
    55	      }
    56	    } else {
    57	      positionals.push(a);
    58	    }
    59	  }
    60	
    61	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(flagTokens, { 'dry-run': 'boolean', 'approve-smoke': 'string' });
    62	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'loop', parsed.error);
    63	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    64	
    65	  const sub = positionals[0];
    66	  if (sub === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'a subcommand is required — try: baton loop init "<goal>" or baton loop run');
    67	  if (sub === 'run' || sub === 'resume') {
    68	    if (positionals.length > 1) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unexpected argument '${positionals[1]}'`);
    69	    if (flags['approve-smoke'] === '') return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', '--approve-smoke requires a value (the token from smoke-approval.json)');
    70	    if (sub === 'resume') flags.__resume = true;
    71	    return runLoop(flags, io);
    72	  }
    73	  if (sub !== 'init') return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unknown subcommand '${sub}' (supported: init, run, resume)`);
    74	
    75	  const goal = positionals[1];
    76	  if (goal === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'loop init requires a goal — baton loop init "<goal>"');
    77	  if (positionals.length > 2) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unexpected argument '${positionals[2]}'`);
    78	
    79	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    80	  const path = `${root}/loop.json`;
    81	
    82	  const finish = (/** @type {any} */ data, /** @type {string} */ human) => {
    83	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data });
    84	    else io.stdout.write(`${human}\n`);
    85	    return 0;
    86	  };
    87	
    88	  // Idempotent: an existing spec is the user's — never overwritten.
    89	  if (io.fs.existsSync(path)) {
    90	    return finish({ created: false, path }, `baton loop init: ${path} already exists — left untouched`);
    91	  }
    92	  if (flags['dry-run'] === true) {
    93	    return finish(
    94	      { created: false, path, dryRun: true },
    95	      `baton loop init (dry-run): would write ${path} — the default baton/loop@1 spec with goal "${goal}"`,
    96	    );
    97	  }
    98	  ensureDir(io.fs, root);
    99	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, path, defaultLoopSpec(goal));
   100	  return finish({ created: true, path }, `baton loop init: wrote ${path} (goal "${goal}") — edit constraints/smoke, then run baton loop run`);
   101	}
   102	
   103	// Exit codes for `loop run` (frozen by the loop-run test contract):
   104	// 0 done / awaiting-smoke-approval · 1 live-lock refusal · 2 usage error ·
   105	// 3 escalated · 4 parked.
   106	const EXIT_ESCALATED = 3;
   107	const EXIT_PARKED = 4;
   108	
   109	/** @param {any} g */
   110	const gitHeadOf = (g) => g?.headSha ?? 'none';
   111	/** @param {any} g */
   112	const gitContentOf = (g) => g?.contentDigest ?? dedupeKey(g ?? null);
   113	
   114	/**
   115	 * Acquire the supervisor run lock ATOMICALLY (exclusive create — never
   116	 * check-then-write, which loses a race by clobbering the winner). A live
   117	 * owner refuses; a provably-dead one is reclaimed: its recorded in-flight
   118	 * child groups (.handoff/loop/children.ndjson) are KILLED first so no
   119	 * orphan survives the takeover, then the lock is retried once.
   120	 * Shared by `loop run` and `pipeline run`.
   121	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {string} cmdLabel
   122	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true, release: () => void} | {ok: false, code: number}>}
   123	 */
   124	export async function acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, cmdLabel) {
   125	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   126	  const lockPath = `${p.dir}/supervisor.lock`;
   127	  const childrenPath = `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`;
   128	  ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   129	  const payload = JSON.stringify({ host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime, runId: `sup-${io.pid}` });
   130	
   131	  const tryExclusive = () => {
   132	    // Fast-path an already-present lock (fakes without O_EXCL semantics rely
   133	    // on this); the wx flag below is the REAL exclusivity on a POSIX fs — a
   134	    // competitor that lands between the check and the write throws EEXIST
   135	    // instead of being clobbered.
   136	    if (io.fs.existsSync(lockPath)) return false;
   137	    try {
   138	      io.fs.writeFileSync(lockPath, payload, { flag: 'wx' });
   139	      return true;
   140	    } catch (err) {
   141	      if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') return false;
   142	      throw err;
   143	    }
   144	  };
   145	
   146	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt += 1) {
   147	    if (tryExclusive()) {
   148	      return {
   149	        ok: true,
   150	        release: () => {
   151	          try {
   152	            if (io.fs.existsSync(lockPath)) io.fs.unlinkSync(lockPath);
   153	          } catch {
   154	            // Best effort — a stale lock is recoverable via the dead path.
   155	          }
   156	        },
   157	      };
   158	    }
   159	    const existing = safeReadJson(io.fs, lockPath);
   160	    const other = existing.ok ? existing.value : null;
   161	    const alive = other && typeof other.pid === 'number' && typeof io.processAlive === 'function' ? io.processAlive(other.pid) : true;
   162	    const sameProcess = other && other.pid === io.pid && other.startTime === io.startTime;
   163	    if (!sameProcess && (!other || other.host !== io.host || alive)) {
   164	      io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: another supervisor (pid ${other?.pid ?? 'unknown'} on ${other?.host ?? 'unknown'}, run ${other?.runId ?? '?'}) holds the run lock — refusing a second supervisor\n`);
   165	      return { ok: false, code: 1 };
   166	    }
   167	    // Provably dead (or our own stale lock): reap its recorded in-flight
   168	    // child groups BEFORE anything else runs, then reclaim.
   169	    if (io.fs.existsSync(childrenPath)) {
   170	      const lines = String(io.fs.readFileSync(childrenPath, 'utf8')).split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim() !== '');
   171	      for (const line of lines) {
   172	        try {
   173	          const rec = JSON.parse(line);
   174	          if (typeof rec?.pgid === 'number' && typeof io.processAlive === 'function' && io.processAlive(rec.pgid)) {
   175	            if (typeof io.processKill === 'function') io.processKill(-rec.pgid, 'SIGKILL');
   176	          }
   177	        } catch {
   178	          // A torn record is unreapable — skip it.
   179	        }
   180	      }
   181	      try {
   182	        io.fs.unlinkSync(childrenPath);
   183	      } catch {
   184	        // Best effort.
   185	      }
   186	    }
   187	    io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: reclaimed the run lock from a provably-dead supervisor (pid ${other?.pid})\n`);
   188	    try {
   189	      io.fs.unlinkSync(lockPath);
   190	    } catch {
   191	      // Already gone.
   192	    }
   193	  }
   194	  io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: could not acquire the run lock after reclaiming — another supervisor keeps winning\n`);
   195	  return { ok: false, code: 1 };
   196	}
   197	
   198	/**
   199	 * The supervisor state machine: drives the spec's phases through headless
   200	 * role children, records every transition in the journal-replayable loop
   201	 * state, enforces the 5-cap, pauses at the smoke gate, and hands limit
   202	 * deaths to the failover transaction. Children run via the injectable seam
   203	 * `io.superviseChild ?? superviseChild`.
   204	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags @param {any} io
   205	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   206	 */
   207	async function runLoop(flags, io) {
   208	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
   209	  const specPath = `${root}/loop.json`;
   210	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   211	  const lockPath = `${p.dir}/supervisor.lock`;
   212	
   213	  // Preconditions — before any lock or spawn.
   214	  const rawSpec = safeReadJson(io.fs, specPath);
   215	  if (!rawSpec.ok) {
   216	    return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `no loop.json at ${specPath} — scaffold one with: baton loop init "<goal>"`);
   217	  }
   218	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   219	  if (!config) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `no readable baton.config.json at ${root} — the role matrix is required`);
   220	  const validated = validateLoopSpec(rawSpec.value, config);
   221	  if (validated.ok !== true) {
   222	    return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `loop.json is invalid:\n  - ${validated.errors.join('\n  - ')}`);
   223	  }
   224	  const spec = validated.spec;
   225	
   226	  // Supervisor run lock — atomic exclusive acquisition; provably-dead owners
   227	  // are reclaimed with their recorded child groups reaped first (B8 + G4).
   228	  const lock = await acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, 'loop run');
   229	  if (lock.ok !== true) return lock.code;
   230	
   231	  // Load or initialize the run state.
   232	  let { state } = await loadLoopState(root, io);
   233	  if (state === null) {
   234	    state = initLoopState(spec, io);
   235	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   236	  }
   237	  const runId = state.runId;
   238	
   239	  /** Apply one event, journal it, persist the snapshot — one transition. */
   240	  const transition = async (/** @type {any} */ ev) => {
   241	    const next = applyLoopEvent(state, ev);
   242	    const seq = await appendLoopEvent(root, ev, io);
   243	    state = { ...next, journalSeq: seq };
   244	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   245	    return state;
   246	  };
   247	
   248	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
   249	  const runner = io.superviseChild ?? superviseChild;
   250	  const sessionHint = `loop-${runId}`;
   251	  /** @type {string[]} */
   252	  let avoid = [];
   253	  /** @type {Array<{platform: string, model: string}>} */
   254	  let avoidEntries = [];
   255	  let childSeq = 0;
   256	
   257	  try {
   258	    // `loop resume` — a PARK is resumable; an escalation is operator-only.
   259	    if (flags.__resume === true) {
   260	      if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   261	        io.stderr.write(`baton loop resume: the run is ESCALATED (gate ${state.escalation?.gate}) — escalation is an operator decision; resolve the findings and start a fresh gate instead\n`);
   262	        return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   263	      }
   264	      if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) {
   265	        await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.RESUME });
   266	        io.stdout.write('baton loop resume: the parked run is running again\n');
   267	      }
   268	    }
   269	
   270	    // --approve-smoke: verify the presented token against RECOMPUTED inputs;
   271	    // drift parks (the human approved a state that no longer exists).
   272	    if (typeof flags['approve-smoke'] === 'string') {
   273	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) {
   274	        return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `--approve-smoke only applies while the run awaits smoke approval (status: ${state.status})`);
   275	      }
   276	      const record = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json`);
   277	      if (!record.ok) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'no smoke-approval.json found — run the loop to the smoke gate first');
   278	      const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   279	      const currentInputs = {
   280	        stateDigest: dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(p.state, 'utf8')),
   281	        smokeCmd: String(spec.smoke?.cmd ?? ''),
   282	        smokeOutputDigest: String(record.value?.inputs?.smokeOutputDigest ?? ''),
   283	        gitHead: gitHeadOf(git),
   284	        gitContentDigest: gitContentOf(git),
   285	        childAssignment: String(record.value?.inputs?.childAssignment ?? ''),
   286	      };
   287	      const verify = verifySmokeToken(String(flags['approve-smoke']), currentInputs);
   288	      if (verify.ok !== true) {
   289	        const drifted = 'driftedInputs' in verify ? verify.driftedInputs.join(', ') : 'unknown';
   290	        await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: `smoke approval token is stale — drifted inputs: ${drifted}; re-run the smoke gate` });
   291	        io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: smoke approval REFUSED — inputs drifted since the token was issued (${drifted}); the run is parked for a fresh smoke pass\n`);
   292	        return EXIT_PARKED;
   293	      }
   294	      await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_APPROVE, token: flags['approve-smoke'], verified: true });
   295	      io.stdout.write('baton loop run: smoke approval verified — continuing the run\n');
   296	    }
   297	
   298	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   299	      io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: the run is escalated (gate ${state.escalation?.gate}) — see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md\n`);
   300	      return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   301	    }
   302	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) {
   303	      io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: the run is parked — ${state.parkReason ?? 'no reason recorded'}\n`);
   304	      return EXIT_PARKED;
   305	    }
   306	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) {
   307	      io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: awaiting smoke approval — resume with: baton loop run --approve-smoke <token from ${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json>\n`);
   308	      return 0;
   309	    }
   310	
   311	    // ---- The phase loop. ---------------------------------------------------
   312	    while (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING && state.phaseIndex < state.phaseCount) {
   313	      const phase = spec.phases[state.phaseIndex];
   314	      const cap = spec.budgets.iterationCap;
   315	      let findings = '';
   316	      let failoverAttempt = 0;
   317	      /** @type {any | null} */
   318	      let forcedAssignment = null;
   319	      /** @type {string | null} */
   320	      let forcedPrompt = null;
   321	      let phaseDone = false;
   322	
   323	      while (!phaseDone) {
   324	        // The cap gates the SPAWN: at the cap the reducer escalates and a
   325	        // 6th child never starts.
   326	        if ((state.iterations?.[phase.id] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   327	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate: phase.id, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   328	          atomicWriteText(
   329	            io.fs,
   330	            `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`,
   331	            `# Loop escalation\n\nGate '${phase.id}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap on run ${runId}.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n\nResolve the findings, then resume with baton loop run.\n`,
   332	          );
   333	          io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: gate '${phase.id}' hit the ${cap}-iteration cap — escalated (see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md)\n`);
   334	          return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   335	        }
   336	        if (childSeq >= spec.budgets.maxChildrenPerPhase * spec.phases.length) {
   337	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: 'total child budget exhausted' });
   338	          return EXIT_PARKED;
   339	        }
   340	
   341	        const resolved =
   342	          forcedAssignment ??
   343	          (() => {
   344	            const r = resolveRoles({ config, to: 'claude-code', avoid, avoidEntries, probes: null }).assignments[phase.role];
   345	            return r && r.mode !== 'unavailable' ? r : null;
   346	          })();
   347	        if (!resolved) {
   348	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: `no eligible platform/model for role '${phase.role}'` });
   349	          io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: no eligible assignment for role '${phase.role}' — parked\n`);
   350	          return EXIT_PARKED;
   351	        }
   352	        const assignment = { ...resolved, role: phase.role };
   353	        const prompt =
   354	          forcedPrompt ??
   355	          [
   356	            `You are the ${phase.role} for loop run ${runId}, phase '${phase.id}'.`,
   357	            `Goal: ${spec.goal}`,
   358	            spec.constraints.length > 0 ? `Constraints:\n${spec.constraints.map((/** @type {string} */ c) => `- ${c}`).join('\n')}` : '',
   359	            findings ? `The previous attempt was BLOCKED with these findings — address every one:\n${findings}` : '',
   360	            "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   361	          ]
   362	            .filter(Boolean)
   363	            .join('\n\n');
   364	        forcedAssignment = null;
   365	        forcedPrompt = null;
   366	
   367	        childSeq += 1;
   368	        const childId = `${String(childSeq).padStart(3, '0')}-${phase.id}`;
   369	        const logPath = `${p.dir}/children/${childId}.log`;
   370	        ensureDir(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children`);
   371	        const childSpec = buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, { root });
   372	        const result = await runner(childSpec, {
   373	          timeoutMs: spec.budgets.perRoleTimeoutMin * 60_000,
   374	          graceMs: 10_000,
   375	          logPath,
   376	          maxLogBytes: 1_000_000,
   377	          platform: assignment.platform,
   378	          // Persist the child's process group the INSTANT it spawns — a
   379	          // supervisor crash must leave every in-flight child reap-able by
   380	          // the reclaiming run (G4).
   381	          onStart: (/** @type {{pid: number, pgid: number}} */ info) => {
   382	            appendEntry(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`, { childId, pid: info.pid, pgid: info.pgid, startedAt: io.now() });
   383	          },
   384	        });
   385	
   386	        // Classification reads the child's LOG (the frozen transcript), so a
   387	        // limit banner routes to failover even when a verdict parsed.
   388	        const transcript = io.fs.existsSync(logPath) ? io.fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf8') : '';
   389	        const cls = classify({ text: transcript, exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 0, platform: assignment.platform, table }).class;
   390	
   391	        if (cls === 'usage-limit' || cls === 'model-unavailable' || cls === 'other-error' || cls === 'throttle' || cls === 'auth') {
   392	          failoverAttempt += 1;
   393	          const decision = await runFailover({
   394	            root,
   395	            io,
   396	            config,
   397	            role: phase.role,
   398	            assignment,
   399	            transcript,
   400	            exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 1,
   401	            sessionHint,
   402	            probes: null,
   403	            avoid,
   404	            avoidEntries,
   405	            attempt: failoverAttempt,
   406	            loopState: { runId, phaseIndex: state.phaseIndex, iterations: state.iterations, status: state.status },
   407	          });
   408	          if (decision.action === 'park') {
   409	            await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: decision.reason });
   410	            io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: parked — ${decision.reason}${'resumeAt' in decision && decision.resumeAt ? ` (resume around ${decision.resumeAt})` : ''}\n`);
   411	            return EXIT_PARKED;
   412	          }
   413	          if (decision.action === 'relaunch') {
   414	            // Platform avoidance is PER-DEATH, not cumulative: runFailover
   415	            // already avoided the just-died platform when it resolved the
   416	            // relaunch. Accumulating here would exhaust every platform on a
   417	            // chained A→B→A failover and park instead of returning to A
   418	            // (acceptance constraint 2). Entry-level avoidance (dead MODELS)
   419	            // does accumulate — a rejected model stays rejected.
   420	            if (Array.isArray(decision.avoidEntries)) avoidEntries = decision.avoidEntries;
   421	            forcedAssignment = { ...decision.assignment, role: phase.role };
   422	            forcedPrompt = typeof decision.prompt === 'string' && decision.prompt.length > 0 ? decision.prompt : null;
   423	            continue; // relaunch the same phase on the new assignment
   424	          }
   425	          continue; // retry: re-spawn the same phase once more
   426	        }
   427	
   428	        const verdict = String(result.verdict ?? 'BLOCKED');
   429	        if (verdict === 'APPROVED' || verdict === 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   430	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE });
   431	          phaseDone = true;
   432	
   433	          // The smoke gate fires right after the smoke-build phase completes.
   434	          if (phase.id === 'smoke-build' && typeof spec.smoke?.cmd === 'string' && spec.smoke.cmd.length > 0) {
   435	            const [cmd, ...cmdArgs] = spec.smoke.cmd.split(/\s+/);
   436	            let smokeOut = '';
   437	            try {
   438	              const r = await io.execFile(cmd, cmdArgs, { cwd: root });
   439	              smokeOut = `${r?.stdout ?? ''}${r?.stderr ?? ''}`;
   440	            } catch (err) {
   441	              smokeOut = `smoke command failed: ${/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err)}`;
   442	            }
   443	            await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_AWAIT });
   444	            const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   445	            const inputs = {
   446	              stateDigest: dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(p.state, 'utf8')),
   447	              smokeCmd: spec.smoke.cmd,
   448	              smokeOutputDigest: dedupeKey(smokeOut),
   449	              gitHead: gitHeadOf(git),
   450	              gitContentDigest: gitContentOf(git),
   451	              childAssignment: JSON.stringify({ platform: assignment.platform, model: assignment.model }),
   452	            };
   453	            const token = smokeApprovalToken(inputs);
   454	            atomicWriteJson(io.fs, `${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json`, { token, inputs, issuedAt: io.now() });
   455	            atomicWriteText(
   456	              io.fs,
   457	              `${p.dir}/SMOKE-REVIEW.md`,
   458	              `# Smoke gate — human approval required\n\nRun: ${runId}\nCommand: \`${spec.smoke.cmd}\`\nExpected: ${spec.smoke.expect ?? '(unspecified)'}\n\n## Output\n\n\`\`\`\n${smokeOut}\n\`\`\`\n\nApprove with:\n\n    baton loop run --approve-smoke ${token}\n\nThe token is bound to the current state/output/git — any drift refuses it.\n`,
   459	            );
   460	            io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: smoke gate reached — review ${p.dir}/SMOKE-REVIEW.md and approve with --approve-smoke <token>\n`);
   461	            return 0;
   462	          }
   463	        } else {
   464	          // BLOCKED (or unparseable, already coerced to BLOCKED upstream).
   465	          findings = String(result.findings ?? '');
   466	          const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate: phase.id, verdict });
   467	          if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   468	            atomicWriteText(
   469	              io.fs,
   470	              `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`,
   471	              `# Loop escalation\n\nGate '${phase.id}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap on run ${runId}.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`,
   472	            );
   473	            io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: gate '${phase.id}' escalated at the cap — see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md\n`);
   474	            return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   475	          }
   476	        }
   477	      }
   478	    }
   479	
   480	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.DONE || state.phaseIndex >= state.phaseCount) {
   481	      io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: done — every phase completed (run ${runId})\n`);
   482	      return 0;
   483	    }
   484	    io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: stopped in status ${state.status}\n`);
   485	    return state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED ? EXIT_PARKED : state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED ? EXIT_ESCALATED : 0;
   486	  } finally {
   487	    // The lock is per-invocation: release on every exit path so a paused run
   488	    // (awaiting approval) can be resumed by the next invocation.
   489	    lock.release();
   490	  }
   491	}

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * Loop failover orchestration — what the supervisor does when a child dies.
     3	 * Classifies the death via the signature table, then takes exactly one path:
     4	 * retry-once-then-park (generic failures), entry-level re-resolve
     5	 * (model-unavailable — the platform survives its dead model), or the
     6	 * usage-limit transaction: checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle,
     7	 * seal, and receive onto the resolver's pick with one bounded stale retry.
     8	 * Writes NOTHING under .handoff/loop/ — the supervisor applies the returned
     9	 * decision to loop state afterward. Plan:
    10	 * docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md §"Limit failover" +
    11	 * §"Model-level failover".
    12	 */
    13	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
    14	import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
    15	import { loadSignatures } from '../detect/signatures.mjs';
    16	import { classify } from '../detect/classifier.mjs';
    17	import { resolveRoles } from '../roles/resolve.mjs';
    18	import { loadBundle } from '../bundle/store.mjs';
    19	import { snapshot as gitSnapshot } from '../git/snapshot.mjs';
    20	import { prepare, commit } from '../receive/txn.mjs';
    21	import { cmdCheckpoint } from '../commands/checkpoint.mjs';
    22	import { cmdFinalize } from '../commands/finalize.mjs';
    23	
    24	const BUILTIN_SIGNATURES = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'data', 'signatures.v1.json');
    25	
    26	/**
    27	 * @param {{
    28	 *   root: string, io: any, config: any, role: string,
    29	 *   assignment: {platform: string, role?: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string},
    30	 *   transcript: string, exitCode: number, sessionHint: string,
    31	 *   probes?: any, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>,
    32	 *   attempt: number, loopState?: any, degradedOpen?: boolean,
    33	 * }} input
    34	 * @returns {Promise<
    35	 *   | {action: 'retry', class: string, attempt: number}
    36	 *   | {action: 'park', class: string, reason: string, resumeAt?: string}
    37	 *   | {action: 'relaunch', class: string, assignment: any, avoidEntries?: any[], prompt?: string}
    38	 * >}
    39	 */
    40	export async function runFailover(input) {
    41	  const { root, io, config, role, assignment, sessionHint } = input;
    42	  const avoid = input.avoid ?? [];
    43	  const avoidEntries = input.avoidEntries ?? [];
    44	
    45	  // Classification is TABLE-driven — the same loader/classifier as `baton
    46	  // detect`, so overlay/fixture signatures are honored, never hardcoded.
    47	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    48	  const verdict = classify({ text: input.transcript, exitCode: input.exitCode, platform: assignment.platform, table });
    49	
    50	  // Model-level failure: the platform is fine, one model is dead. Avoid the
    51	  // exact {platform, model} tuple and re-resolve — no seal, no receive.
    52	  if (verdict.class === 'model-unavailable') {
    53	    const nextAvoidEntries = [...avoidEntries, { platform: assignment.platform, model: assignment.model }];
    54	    const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    55	    const next = resolved.assignments[role];
    56	    if (!next || next.mode === 'unavailable') {
    57	      return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `no eligible chain entry left for role '${role}' after avoiding ${assignment.platform}/${assignment.model}` };
    58	    }
    59	    return { action: 'relaunch', class: verdict.class, assignment: next, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries };
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  // Anything that is not a usage-limit death is a child failure, not a
    63	  // platform death: retry once, then park. Never a seal or receive.
    64	  if (verdict.class !== 'usage-limit') {
    65	    if (input.attempt <= 1) return { action: 'retry', class: verdict.class, attempt: input.attempt };
    66	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `child failed twice (${verdict.class}) — parked for operator review` };
    67	  }
    68	
    69	  // ---- Usage-limit: the exact transaction (plan steps 3–8). ----------------
    70	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
    71	  const originPlatform = bundle?.origin?.platform ?? assignment.platform;
    72	
    73	  // (3) Checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle under the supervisor
    74	  // session BEFORE any seal, so the frozen seal carries it.
    75	  if (input.loopState !== undefined) {
    76	    const checkpointIo = {
    77	      ...io,
    78	      stdin: JSON.stringify({
    79	        schema: 'baton/event@1',
    80	        events: [{ type: 'decision', payload: { summary: `loop position at limit death: ${JSON.stringify(input.loopState)}` } }],
    81	      }),
    82	    };
    83	    await cmdCheckpoint(['--platform', originPlatform, '--session', sessionHint, '--root', root], checkpointIo);
    84	  }
    85	
    86	  // (4) Seal — unless the caller knows a clean seal is impossible
    87	  // (degradedOpen: a prior death left the bundle unsealed; receive's
    88	  // degraded-open path compensates), or the bundle is already sealed.
    89	  const alreadySealed = bundle?.handoff?.status === 'sealed';
    90	  if (input.degradedOpen !== true && !alreadySealed) {
    91	    await cmdFinalize(['--reason', 'usage-limit death during a supervised loop run', '--reason-class', 'usage-limit', '--root', root], io);
    92	  }
    93	
    94	  // (7, ordered before receive because receive needs the target) — resolver
    95	  // pick with the dead origin platform avoided.
    96	  const relaunchAvoid = avoid.includes(assignment.platform) ? avoid : [...avoid, assignment.platform];
    97	  const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid: relaunchAvoid, avoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    98	  const target = resolved.assignments[role];
    99	  if (!target || target.mode === 'unavailable') {
   100	    return {
   101	      action: 'park',
   102	      class: verdict.class,
   103	      reason: `every platform is avoided or unavailable for role '${role}' — parked with a resume hint`,
   104	      ...(verdict.resetHint ? { resumeAt: verdict.resetHint } : {}),
   105	    };
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  // (5–6) Receive prepare+commit back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake and the
   109	  // supervisor session hint. Git is re-derived fresh for each phase (exactly
   110	  // as the CLI does), so real drift inside the window stales the token; ONE
   111	  // automatic re-prepare retry, then park. No .handoff/loop writes anywhere.
   112	  const receiveOpts = (/** @type {any} */ git) => ({
   113	    platform: target.platform,
   114	    origin: 'unknown', // defaults from the sealed bundle's recorded origin
   115	    reason: 'unspecified', // defaults from the sealed reason
   116	    reasonClass: 'usage-limit',
   117	    gitSnapshot: git,
   118	    probes: input.probes ?? null,
   119	    sessionHint,
   120	    sessionUnstable: false,
   121	  });
   122	
   123	  /** @type {string} */
   124	  let prompt = '';
   125	  let lastError = null;
   126	  for (let window = 1; window <= 2; window += 1) {
   127	    const prepGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   128	    const prepared = prepare(root, receiveOpts(prepGit), io);
   129	    prompt = prepared.prompt;
   130	    const commitGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   131	    try {
   132	      commit(root, prepared.token, receiveOpts(commitGit), io);
   133	      lastError = null;
   134	      break;
   135	    } catch (err) {
   136	      lastError = err;
   137	    }
   138	  }
   139	  if (lastError !== null) {
   140	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (lastError)?.message ?? String(lastError);
   141	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `receive commit stayed stale after one re-prepare retry — ${msg}` };
   142	  }
   143	
   144	  // (8) Relaunch on the adopted platform with the resume prompt.
   145	  return {
   146	    action: 'relaunch',
   147	    class: verdict.class,
   148	    assignment: target,
   149	    avoidEntries,
   150	    prompt,
   151	  };
   152	}

   478	// B8 (G2) — the run-lock acquisition must be ATOMIC, not check-then-write.
   479	describe('loop run — atomic run-lock acquisition (B8)', () => {
   480	  const DIR = `${loopPaths('/repo').dir}`;
   481	  const LOCK = `${DIR}/supervisor.lock`;
   482	
   483	  it('RED (B8): implementation-neutral — the competitor materializes AT the exclusive-create; wx/mkdir-first refuses, check-then-write clobbers (RED)', async () => {
   484	    const io = makeLoopRepo({ runner: undefined });
   485	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [{ verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'APPROVED' }]);
   486	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   487	    io.processAlive = (p) => p === 55555; // the competitor supervisor is LIVE
   488	
   489	    const realWrite = io.fs.writeFileSync.bind(io.fs);
   490	    const realMkdir = io.fs.mkdirSync.bind(io.fs);
   491	    const realRename = io.fs.renameSync.bind(io.fs);
   492	    const COMPETITOR = JSON.stringify({ host: 'loop-host', pid: 55555, startTime: 222, runId: 'competitor' });
   493	
   494	    // The competitor wins the lock the INSTANT before the supervisor's own write
   495	    // to LOCK lands — injected at whichever primitive the acquire uses to create
   496	    // it. NO readFileSync hook, so a wx/mkdir-FIRST acquire (which never reads
   497	    // before creating) cannot dodge the race.
   498	    let injected = false;
   499	    const injectBefore = (/** @type {any} */ target) => {
   500	      if (injected || String(target) !== LOCK) return;
   501	      injected = true;
   502	      realMkdir(DIR, { recursive: true });
   503	      realWrite(LOCK, COMPETITOR);
   504	    };
   505	
   506	    // Exclusive create (flag wx/ax) enforces the O_EXCL semantics memfs lacks:
   507	    // once the competitor exists, an exclusive write throws EEXIST.
   508	    io.fs.writeFileSync = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ data, /** @type {any} */ opts) => {
   509	      const flag = typeof opts === 'string' ? undefined : opts?.flag;
   510	      const exclusive = flag === 'wx' || flag === 'ax' || flag === 'wx+' || flag === 'ax+';
   511	      injectBefore(p);
   512	      if (exclusive && String(p) === LOCK && io.fs.existsSync(p)) throw Object.assign(new Error(`EEXIST: file already exists, open '${p}'`), { code: 'EEXIST' });
   513	      return realWrite(p, data, opts); // a PLAIN write to LOCK clobbers the competitor
   514	    };
   515	    // mkdirSync(LOCK) as an exclusive lock dir: memfs already throws EEXIST when a
   516	    // node exists at the path (the injected competitor file).
   517	    io.fs.mkdirSync = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ opts) => { injectBefore(p); return realMkdir(p, opts); };
   518	    // A tmp+rename publish (atomicWriteJson) clobbers the competitor on rename.
   519	    io.fs.renameSync = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { injectBefore(to); return realRename(from, to); };
   520

   107	/**
   108	 * A STRICT, stateful fake git: unstubbed commands reject; worktree add/list and
   109	 * checkout -b are modeled so setup + preflight/postflight + merge cohere.
   110	 * `over` overrides specific responses (e.g. a merge conflict).
   111	 */
   112	function pipelineGit({ over = {}, log = CLEAN_LOG, existingBranches = [], dirtyCwds = [] } = {}) {
   113	  const added = /** @type {Map<string,string>} */ (new Map()); // path -> branch
   114	  const branchAt = /** @type {Map<string,string>} */ (new Map()); // cwd -> current branch
   115	  const branches = new Set(existingBranches); // stale/pre-existing namespaced branches
   116	  const dirty = new Set(dirtyCwds); // seat cwds whose index is dirty
   117	  const deleted = new Set(); // seats listed by git but raw-deleted on disk
   118	  const calls = /** @type {any[]} */ ([]);
   119	  const lockProbeRef = { fn: /** @type {null | (() => boolean)} */ (null) };
   120	  let mainSha = MAIN_SHA; // mutable so a child can "move main" mid-subtask
   121	
   122	  const list = () => {
   123	    const entries = [{ path: '/repo', branch: 'main' }];
   124	    for (const [path, branch] of added) entries.push({ path, branch: branchAt.get(path) ?? branch });
   125	    return entries.map((e) => `worktree ${e.path}\nHEAD ${MAIN_SHA}\nbranch refs/heads/${e.branch}\n`).join('\n');
   126	  };
   127	
   128	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = [], /** @type {any} */ opts = {}) => {
   129	    const argstr = args.join(' ');
   130	    calls.push({ cmd, args, argstr, cwd: opts?.cwd, lockPresent: lockProbeRef.fn ? lockProbeRef.fn() : undefined });
   131	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   132	
   133	    // Explicit overrides win.
   134	    const okey = Object.keys(over).sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length).find((k) => argstr.includes(k));
   135	    if (okey) {
   136	      const r = over[okey];
   137	      if (r?.reject) return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(r.stderr || 'git failed'), { code: r.code ?? 1, stdout: r.stdout ?? '', stderr: r.stderr ?? '' }));
   138	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: r?.stdout ?? '', stderr: r?.stderr ?? '' });
   139	    }
   140	
   141	    // A raw-deleted seat: git still LISTS it, but any command IN that cwd fails
   142	    // (the directory is gone). Only self-heal (prune + re-add) recovers it.
   143	    if (opts?.cwd && deleted.has(opts.cwd) && !argstr.startsWith('worktree ')) {
   144	      return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(`fatal: cannot chdir to '${opts.cwd}': No such file or directory`), { code: 128, stderr: 'No such file or directory\n' }));
   145	    }
   146	    if (argstr.startsWith('worktree list')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: list(), stderr: '' });
   147	    if (argstr.startsWith('worktree add')) {
   148	      const path = args.find((a) => a.startsWith('/repo/.worktrees/'));
   149	      const bi = args.indexOf('-b');
   150	      const branch = bi >= 0 ? args[bi + 1] : 'baton/wt-x/base';
   151	      if (path) { added.set(path, branch); branchAt.set(path, branch); deleted.delete(path); }
   152	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: '', stderr: '' });
   153	    }
   154	    if (argstr.startsWith('worktree prune')) { deleted.clear(); return Promise.resolve({ stdout: '', stderr: '' }); }
   155	    if (argstr.startsWith('worktree remove')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: '', stderr: '' });
   156	    if (argstr.startsWith('checkout -b')) {
   157	      const target = args[args.indexOf('-b') + 1];
   158	      if (branches.has(target)) return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(`fatal: a branch named '${target}' already exists`), { code: 128, stderr: `fatal: a branch named '${target}' already exists\n` }));
   159	      branches.add(target);
   160	      if (opts?.cwd) branchAt.set(opts.cwd, target);
   161	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: '', stderr: '' });
   162	    }
   163	    if (argstr.startsWith('status --porcelain')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: dirty.has(opts?.cwd) ? ' M dirty.txt\n' : '', stderr: '' });
   164	    if (argstr === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD') return Promise.resolve({ stdout: `${branchAt.get(opts?.cwd) ?? 'main'}\n`, stderr: '' });
   165	    if (argstr.startsWith('rev-parse')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: `${mainSha}\n`, stderr: '' });
   166	    if (argstr.startsWith('log ')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: log, stderr: '' });
   167	    if (argstr.startsWith('merge')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: 'Fast-forward', stderr: '' });
   168	    if (argstr.startsWith('branch -D')) return Promise.resolve({ stdout: '', stderr: '' });
   169	    return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(`unstubbed git: ${argstr}`), { code: 'ENOSTUB' }));
   170	  };
   171	  fn.calls = calls;
   172	  fn.git = () => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git');
   173	  fn.issued = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re) => calls.some((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr));
   174	  fn.matching = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re) => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr));
   175	  fn.withCwd = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re, /** @type {string} */ cwd) => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr) && c.cwd === cwd);
   176	  fn.setLockProbe = (/** @type {() => boolean} */ f) => { lockProbeRef.fn = f; };
   177	  fn.moveMain = (/** @type {string} */ sha) => { mainSha = sha; }; // a child "moves main" mid-subtask
   178	  fn.setBranch = (/** @type {string} */ cwd, /** @type {string} */ branch) => { branchAt.set(cwd, branch); };
   179	  // Explicit seed: git LISTS this worktree; `raw` marks its dir as deleted on
   180	  // disk (any in-cwd command fails until prune + re-add self-heals it).
   181	  fn.seedWorktree = (/** @type {string} */ path, /** @type {string} */ branch, /** @type {{raw?: boolean}} */ o = {}) => {
   182	    added.set(path, branch);
   183	    branchAt.set(path, branch);
   184	    if (o.raw) deleted.add(path);
   185	  };
   186	  return fn;
   187	}
   188	
   189	function fakeRunner(io, script) {
   190	  const queue = [...script];
   191	  const calls = /** @type {any[]} */ ([]);
   192	  const fn = (/** @type {any} */ spec, /** @type {any} */ opts = {}) => {
   193	    calls.push({ spec, opts, command: spec?.command, args: spec?.args ?? [], env: spec?.env });
   194	    const r = queue.shift() ?? { verdict: 'APPROVED' };
   195	    if (typeof r.logContent === 'string' && opts.logPath) {
   196	      const dir = opts.logPath.slice(0, opts.logPath.lastIndexOf('/'));
   197	      io.fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
   198	      io.fs.writeFileSync(opts.logPath, r.logContent);
   199	    }
   200	    // A child may perturb the world (e.g. move main) between spawn and postflight.
   201	    if (typeof r.effect === 'function') r.effect();
   202	    return Promise.resolve({ timedOut: false, exitCode: r.exitCode ?? 0, verdict: r.verdict ?? 'APPROVED', findings: r.findings ?? '', logPath: opts.logPath });
   203	  };
   204	  fn.calls = calls;
   205	  return fn;
   206	}
   207	
   208	function makePipeRepo({ spec = pipelineSpec(), config = PIPELINE_CONFIG, files = {}, git, runner, env = {} } = {}) {
   209	  const io = makeIo({
   210	    now: T0,
   211	    host: 'pipe-host',
   212	    pid: 4242,
   213	    startTime: 111000,
   214	    env,
   215	    files: {
   216	      [SIG_ABS]: SIG_CONTENT,
   217	      '/repo/.git/HEAD': 'ref: refs/heads/main\n',
   218	      '/repo/baton.config.json': JSON.stringify(config, null, 2),
   219	      ...(spec ? { '/repo/loop.json': JSON.stringify(spec, null, 2) + '\n' } : {}),
   220	      ...files,

exec
/bin/zsh -lc "nl -ba tests/commands/pipeline-run.test.mjs | sed -n '220,520p'" in /Users/saksham/baton
exec
/bin/zsh -lc "nl -ba tests/commands/pipeline-run.test.mjs | sed -n '520,820p'" in /Users/saksham/baton
 succeeded in 0ms:
   220	      ...files,
   221	    },
   222	  });
   223	  const g = git ?? pipelineGit();
   224	  g.setLockProbe(() => io.fs.existsSync(MERGE_LOCK));
   225	  io.execFile = g;
   226	  const fake = runner ?? fakeRunner(io, []);
   227	  io.superviseChild = fake;
   228	  io.__git = g;
   229	  io.__runner = fake;
   230	  return io;
   231	}
   232	
   233	// A full clean subtask = writer APPROVED, reviewer APPROVED, merger APPROVED.
   234	const cleanSubtask = () => [{ verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'APPROVED' }];
   235	const argsOf = (call) => (call?.args ?? []).map(String);
   236	const valAfter = (arr, flag) => { const i = arr.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? arr[i + 1] : undefined; };
   237	const childWithModel = (runner, model) => runner.calls.filter((c) => argsOf(c).includes(model));
   238	// Writers = the write-capable children (in call order). Reviewers = read-only
   239	// children whose prompt carries the 'subtask-reviewer' role identity (so the
   240	// merger, also read-only, is excluded).
   241	const writersOf = (runner) => runner.calls.filter((c) => valAfter(argsOf(c), '-s') === 'workspace-write');
   242	const reviewersOf = (runner) => runner.calls.filter((c) => valAfter(argsOf(c), '-s') === 'read-only' && argsOf(c).join(' ').includes('subtask-reviewer'));

   391	describe('pipeline — verdict flow', () => {
   392	  it('reviewer APPROVED -> the MERGER child runs (merger model); on its APPROVED the SUPERVISOR merges via mergeSubtask', async () => {
   393	    const io = makePipeRepo({ runner: undefined });
   394	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [...cleanSubtask(), ...cleanSubtask()]);
   395	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   396	    await run(['pipeline', 'run'], io);
   397	
   398	    // The merger child ran on the merger chain model and is NON-git-capable
   399	    // (read-only) — it can re-check but never merge itself (finding 4).
   400	    const mergers = childWithModel(io.__runner, 'mg-model');
   401	    assert.ok(mergers.length >= 1, 'the merger role child runs after APPROVED');
   402	    assert.equal(valAfter(argsOf(mergers[0]), '-s'), 'read-only', 'the merger child is read-only — it cannot write/merge itself');
   403	
   404	    // The REAL merge happened through mergeSubtask (the supervisor). EVERY merge
   405	    // and ff-only call carries the supervisor shape: merge at /repo, ff-only in a
   406	    // seat cwd, all under the acquired merge lock.
   407	    const m1 = io.__git.matching(/^merge baton\/wt-a\/subtask-t1$/);
   408	    assert.equal(m1.length, 1, 'the subtask-1 branch is merged exactly once');
   409	    for (const c of io.__git.matching(/^merge baton\//)) {
   410	      assert.equal(c.cwd, '/repo', 'every subtask merge runs at the repo root');
   411	      assert.equal(c.lockPresent, true, 'every subtask merge runs under the merge lock');
   412	    }
   413	    const ff = io.__git.matching(/^merge --ff-only main$/);
   414	    assert.ok(ff.length >= 2, 'both worktrees fast-forward to main after each merge');
   415	    for (const c of ff) {
   416	      assert.ok(c.cwd === WT_A || c.cwd === WT_B, 'every ff-only sync runs in a seat worktree cwd');
   417	      assert.equal(c.lockPresent, true, 'every ff-only sync runs under the merge lock');
   418	    }
   419	  });
   420	
   421	  it('reviewer BLOCKED -> the SAME writer seat re-runs with the findings in its prompt', async () => {
   422	    const io = makePipeRepo({ runner: undefined });
   423	    // subtask 1: writer APPROVED, reviewer BLOCKED (findings), then writer re-run APPROVED, reviewer APPROVED, merger APPROVED; then subtask 2 clean.
   424	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [
   425	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, // writer 1
   426	      { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'REVIEW-FINDING-X' }, // reviewer 1
   427	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, // writer 1 re-run
   428	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, // reviewer 1 again
   429	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, // merger 1
   430	      ...cleanSubtask(), // subtask 2
   431	    ]);
   432	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   433	    await run(['pipeline', 'run'], io);
   434	    // The re-run writer (2nd wa-model writer in wt-a) carries the findings.
   435	    const writers = childWithModel(io.__runner, 'wa-model').filter((c) => valAfter(argsOf(c), '-s') === 'workspace-write');
   436	    assert.ok(writers.length >= 2, 'the writer seat re-ran after the BLOCKED review');
   437	    assert.match(argsOf(writers[1]).join(' '), /REVIEW-FINDING-X/, "the re-run writer's prompt carries the review findings");
   438	  });

   440	  it('review-gate cap exhaustion -> escalated, ESCALATION.md, exit 3, no 6th spawn', async () => {
   441	    const io = makePipeRepo({ runner: undefined });
   442	    // Reviewer BLOCKS five times; the 6th writer/reviewer pair must never spawn.
   443	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [
   444	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f1' },
   445	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f2' },
   446	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f3' },
   447	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f4' },
   448	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f5' },
   449	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: 'f6' }, // must NEVER be consumed
   450	    ]);
   451	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   452	    const code = await run(['pipeline', 'run'], io);
   453	    assert.equal(code, 3, 'a per-subtask review gate at the cap escalates');
   454	    assert.ok(loopFile(io, 'ESCALATION.md'), 'an ESCALATION.md is written');
   455	    // Exactly five writer+reviewer cycles ran — the 6th pair (and the f6 result)
   456	    // are never consumed, and the merger never runs (finding 3).
   457	    assert.equal(io.__runner.calls.length, 10, 'exactly 5 writers + 5 reviewers before escalation — no 6th spawn');
   458	    assert.equal(writersOf(io.__runner).length, 5, 'five writer attempts');
   459	    assert.equal(reviewersOf(io.__runner).length, 5, 'five review attempts');
   460	    assert.equal(childWithModel(io.__runner, 'mg-model').length, 0, 'the merger never runs for an escalated subtask');
   461	    const { state } = await loadLoopState('/repo', io);
   462	    assert.equal(state.status, LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED, 'the escalation is persisted to loop state');
   463	  });

   465	  it('merger BLOCKED -> the writer retries (same gate-cap discipline)', async () => {

   471	      { verdict: 'APPROVED' }, // writer re-run

   480	  });

   542	    // The writer child (first spawn) moves main between preflight-capture and postflight.

     1	/**
     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
    58	  /** @param {any} m */
    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>
    62	    avoidEntries.some((a) => a?.platform === platform && baseModel(a?.model) === baseModel(model));
    63	
    64	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    65	  const assignments = {};
    66	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
    67	    /** @type {any[]} */
    68	    const skipped = [];
    69	    /** @type {any} */
    70	    let assignment = null;
    71	
    72	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    73	      const entry = chain[i];
    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    76	        continue;
    77	      }
    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    79	      if (why) {
    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    81	        continue;
    82	      }
    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
    86	        continue;
    87	      }
    88	      assignment = {
    89	        platform: entry.platform,
    90	        model: entry.model,
    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    93	        chainIndex: i,
    94	        skipped,
    95	      };
    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    97	      break;
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
   107	      }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    if (!assignment) {
   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   112	    }
   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  return { assignments, notes };
   117	}

   507	    // once the competitor exists, an exclusive write throws EEXIST.
   508	    io.fs.writeFileSync = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ data, /** @type {any} */ opts) => {
   509	      const flag = typeof opts === 'string' ? undefined : opts?.flag;
   510	      const exclusive = flag === 'wx' || flag === 'ax' || flag === 'wx+' || flag === 'ax+';
   511	      injectBefore(p);
   512	      if (exclusive && String(p) === LOCK && io.fs.existsSync(p)) throw Object.assign(new Error(`EEXIST: file already exists, open '${p}'`), { code: 'EEXIST' });
   513	      return realWrite(p, data, opts); // a PLAIN write to LOCK clobbers the competitor
   514	    };
   515	    // mkdirSync(LOCK) as an exclusive lock dir: memfs already throws EEXIST when a
   516	    // node exists at the path (the injected competitor file).
   517	    io.fs.mkdirSync = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ opts) => { injectBefore(p); return realMkdir(p, opts); };
   518	    // A tmp+rename publish (atomicWriteJson) clobbers the competitor on rename.
   519	    io.fs.renameSync = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { injectBefore(to); return realRename(from, to); };
   520	
   521	    const code = await cmdLoop(['run'], io);
   522	    assert.equal(code, 1, 'a wx/mkdir-first exclusive acquire observes EEXIST and refuses the run');
   523	    assert.equal(io.__runner.calls.length, 0, 'no child spawned when the lock was lost to the competitor');
   524	    assert.match(JSON.parse(io.files()[LOCK]).runId, /competitor/, "the competitor's lock is not clobbered (a check-then-write path fails here)");
   525	  });
   526	});
   527	
   528	// ===========================================================================
   529	// G4 (A4) — record in-flight child groups; kill recorded orphans on reclaim.
   530	describe('loop run — child-group recording + kill-on-reclaim (G4)', () => {
   531	  const DIR = `${loopPaths('/repo').dir}`;
   532	
   533	  const readChildren = (io) => {
   534	    const raw = io.files()[`${DIR}/children.ndjson`];
   535	    if (typeof raw !== 'string') return [];
   536	    return raw.split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim() !== '').map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
   537	  };
   538	
   539	  it('RED (G4): a child-start record {childId, pid, pgid, startedAt} exists on disk WHILE the child is in flight (before completion)', async () => {
   540	    const io = makeLoopRepo({ runner: undefined });
   541	    let n = 0;
   542	    const inflightOk = [];
   543	    // The runner reports the child's group via opts.onStart (spawn time); the
   544	    // supervisor must persist the record synchronously in that handler — BEFORE
   545	    // the child completes — so a mid-run crash leaves the orphan reap-able.
   546	    io.superviseChild = (/** @type {any} */ _spec, /** @type {any} */ opts) => {
   547	      n += 1;
   548	      const info = { pid: 8000 + n, pgid: 9000 + n };
   549	      if (typeof opts.onStart === 'function') opts.onStart(info);
   550	      const rec = readChildren(io).find((r) => r.pgid === info.pgid);
   551	      inflightOk.push(
   552	        !!rec && typeof rec.childId === 'string' && rec.childId.length > 0 && rec.pid === info.pid && typeof rec.startedAt === 'string' && rec.startedAt.length > 0,
   553	      );
   554	      return Promise.resolve({ timedOut: false, exitCode: 0, verdict: 'APPROVED', findings: '', logPath: opts.logPath, ...info });
   555	    };
   556	    const code = await cmdLoop(['run'], io);
   557	    assert.equal(code, 0);
   558	    assert.ok(inflightOk.length >= 1, 'at least one child ran');
   559	    assert.ok(inflightOk.every(Boolean), 'each child-start record ({childId,pid,pgid,startedAt}) existed on disk while its child was in flight');
   560	  });
   561	
   562	  it('RED (G5/G4): on dead-lock reclaim, a still-alive recorded orphan group is KILLED (io.processKill) BEFORE the first new spawn', async () => {
   563	    const io = makeLoopRepo({ runner: undefined });
   564	    const events = []; // ordered: kills and spawns interleaved
   565	    io.processKill = (/** @type {number} */ pid, /** @type {any} */ sig) => { events.push({ kind: 'kill', pid, sig }); return true; };
   566	    const baseRunner = fakeRunner(io, [{ verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'APPROVED' }]);
   567	    io.superviseChild = (/** @type {any} */ spec, /** @type {any} */ opts) => { events.push({ kind: 'spawn' }); return baseRunner(spec, opts); };
   568	    io.__runner = baseRunner;
   569	    // The dead supervisor's orphan group (pgid 9001) is still alive; its lock is dead.
   570	    io.processAlive = (/** @type {number} */ p) => p === 9001;
   571	    io.fs.mkdirSync(DIR, { recursive: true });
   572	    io.fs.writeFileSync(`${DIR}/supervisor.lock`, JSON.stringify({ host: 'loop-host', pid: 999999, startTime: 7, runId: 'crashed' }));
   573	    io.fs.writeFileSync(`${DIR}/children.ndjson`, JSON.stringify({ childId: '001-plan', pid: 8001, pgid: 9001, startedAt: T0 }) + '\n');
   574	
   575	    const code = await cmdLoop(['run'], io);
   576	    assert.equal(code, 0, `the reclaiming run completes after reaping orphans; stderr: ${io.stderrText()}`);
   577	    const firstSpawn = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'spawn');
   578	    const killIdx = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'kill' && Math.abs(e.pid) === 9001);
   579	    assert.ok(killIdx >= 0, `the orphan group 9001 was killed on reclaim; events: ${JSON.stringify(events)}`);
   580	    assert.ok(firstSpawn === -1 || killIdx < firstSpawn, 'the orphan group was killed BEFORE the first new child spawned');
   581	  });
   582	});
   583	
   584	// ===========================================================================
   585	// G6 (B6) — `baton loop resume`: PARKED -> running; ESCALATED refused.
   586	describe('loop run — resume (G6)', () => {
   587	  const DIR = `${loopPaths('/repo').dir}`;
   588	  const seedState = (over) => ({
   589	    schema: 'baton/loop-state@1',
   590	    runId: 'loop-r',
   591	    goal: 'Ship the loop',
   592	    phaseCount: 2,
   593	    phaseIndex: 0,
   594	    iterations: {},
   595	    status: 'running',
   596	    parkReason: null,
   597	    escalation: null,
   598	    smokeApproval: null,
   599	    createdAt: T0,
   600	    journalSeq: 0,
   601	    ...over,
   602	  });
   603	
   604	  it('RED (G6): `baton loop resume` transitions a PARKED run back to running and continues (spawns the pending phase)', async () => {
   605	    const io = makeLoopRepo({ runner: undefined });
   606	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [{ verdict: 'APPROVED' }, { verdict: 'APPROVED' }]);
   607	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   608	    io.fs.mkdirSync(DIR, { recursive: true });
   609	    io.fs.writeFileSync(`${DIR}/state.json`, JSON.stringify(seedState({ status: 'parked', parkReason: 'operator paused' }), null, 2) + '\n');
   610	
   611	    const code = await cmdLoop(['resume'], io);
   612	    assert.equal(code, 0, `resume continues a parked run; stderr: ${io.stderrText()}`);
   613	    assert.ok(io.__runner.calls.length >= 1, 'resume spawned the pending phase');
   614	    assert.equal((await loadLoopState('/repo', io)).state.status, LOOP_STATUS.DONE, 'the resumed run completes');
   615	  });
   616	
   617	  it('RED (G6): resume on an ESCALATED run is REFUSED (escalation stays operator-only, no spawn)', async () => {
   618	    const io = makeLoopRepo({ runner: undefined });
   619	    io.superviseChild = fakeRunner(io, [{ verdict: 'APPROVED' }]);
   620	    io.__runner = io.superviseChild;
   621	    io.fs.mkdirSync(DIR, { recursive: true });
   622	    io.fs.writeFileSync(`${DIR}/state.json`, JSON.stringify(seedState({ status: 'escalated', escalation: { gate: 'gate-1', iteration: 5 } }), null, 2) + '\n');
   623	
   624	    const code = await cmdLoop(['resume'], io);
   625	    assert.notEqual(code, 0, 'an escalated run cannot be resumed');
   626	    assert.match(io.stderrText() + io.stdoutText(), /escalat|operator/i, 'the refusal explains escalation is operator-only');
   627	    assert.equal(io.__runner.calls.length, 0, 'resume never spawns on an escalated run');
   628	    assert.equal((await loadLoopState('/repo', io)).state.status, LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED, 'the run stays escalated');
   629	  });

    21	// PINNED EXPORT (implementer follows): runFailover(input) -> Promise<decision>
    22	//   input = { root, io, config, role, assignment, transcript, exitCode,
    23	//             sessionHint, probes, avoid, avoidEntries, attempt, loopState,
    24	//             degradedOpen? }
    25	//     degradedOpen (default false): the supervisor could NOT cleanly seal (a
    26	//     prior limit death left the bundle unsealed). runFailover then SKIPS
    27	//     finalize and takes receive's degraded-open path (no .finalize.json freeze;
    28	//     the receive generates a degraded seal). The default alive path checkpoints
    29	//     -> finalize (seals) -> sealed receive.
    30	//   decision = { action: 'retry'|'park'|'relaunch', class, ... }:
    31	//     retry     -> { action:'retry', class, attempt }
    32	//     park      -> { action:'park', class, reason, resumeAt? }
    33	//     relaunch  -> { action:'relaunch', class, assignment, avoidEntries?, prompt? }
    34	//
    35	// Window drift (finding 5) is expressed purely through io.execFile SEQUENCING
    36	// (git rev-parse HEAD returning different values on successive calls) — the
    37	// production receive path re-derives git for prepare and for commit, so a HEAD
    38	// change between them stales the token. There is NO test-only hook.
    39	//
    40	// RED MECHANISM: dynamic-import-with-catch + M() guard (meaningful reds).

   141	// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
   142	// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
   143	// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
   144	function gitExec(headForCall) {
   145	  let headCalls = 0;
   146	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   147	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   148	    const key = args.join(' ');
   149	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   150	      headCalls += 1;
   151	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   152	    }
   153	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   154	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   155	  };
   156	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   157	  return fn;
   158	}

   160	// Spy every write touching .handoff/loop.
   161	function spyLoopWrites(io) {
   162	  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
   163	  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
   164	  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
   165	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   166	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
   167	  }
   168	  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
   169	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   170	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
   171	  }
   172	  return writes;
   173	}

   175	const historyFreezes = (io) => {
   176	  const dir = bundlePaths('/repo').historyDir;
   177	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
   178	  // Parse ONLY snapshot freezes (.json). rotateJournalIn also writes .ndjson
   179	  // journal freezes here — legitimately empty or multi-line — which are not JSON.
   180	  return io.fs
   181	    .readdirSync(dir)
   182	    .filter((/** @type {string} */ n) => n.endsWith('.json'))
   183	    .map((/** @type {string} */ n) => ({ name: n, data: JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(`${dir}/${n}`, 'utf8')) }));
   184	};

   364	    // to write AFTER, from the returned decision. This subsumes the prepare->commit
   365	    // window (no loop write anywhere in the failover).
   366	    assert.deepEqual(loopWrites, [], `the failover transaction must not write under .handoff/loop; wrote: ${JSON.stringify(loopWrites)}`);
   367	  });

   369	  it('(f) the relaunch decision carries the resolver assignment (dead origin avoided) and a resume prompt', async () => {

   377	  });

   382	    const b = await runFailover(usageLimitInput(makeRepoIo({ status: 'open' })));
   383	    assert.deepEqual(a.assignment, b.assignment, 'the relaunch target is deterministic');
   384	    assert.equal(a.action, b.action);
   385	  });
   386	});

   389	describe('runFailover — usage-limit: git drift between prepare and commit (e), via io.execFile', () => {
   390	  // Drift tests seed an ALREADY-SEALED bundle and pass no new loopState, so the
   391	  // only git consumers are receive's prepare + commit — each HEAD read maps 1:1
   392	  // onto a prepare/commit call, with no leading finalize/checkpoint git.
   393	  const driftInput = (io) => usageLimitInput(io, { loopState: undefined });
   394	
   395	  it('git moves ONCE between prepare and its commit -> first commit stale -> ONE re-prepare+commit succeeds', async () => {
   396	    const { runFailover } = M();
   397	    // calls: 1=prepare(A) 2=commit(B, differs -> stale) 3=re-prepare(stable) 4=re-commit(stable, matches)
   398	    const git = gitExec((n) => (n === 1 ? 'HEAD-A' : n === 2 ? 'HEAD-B' : 'HEAD-STABLE'));
   399	    const io = makeRepoIo({ status: 'sealed', execFile: git });
   400	    const d = await runFailover(driftInput(io));
   401	    assert.equal(d.action, 'relaunch', 'the single automatic retry recovers from the one-time drift');
   402	    assert.equal(loadBundle('/repo', io).bundle.generation, 2, 'the retried commit landed');
   403	  });
   404

   406	    const { runFailover } = M();

   408	    const git = gitExec((n) => `HEAD-${n}`);
   409	    const io = makeRepoIo({ status: 'sealed', execFile: git });

   411	    assert.equal(d.action, 'park', 'two consecutive stale commits park instead of looping');
   412	    assert.match(String(d.reason), /stale|drift|re-?prepare/i, 'the park reason names the drift');
   413	    assert.equal(loadBundle('/repo', io).bundle.generation, 1, 'no generation opened when the failover parked');

   415	    // bounded-3+ loop would read 6+ (finding 3).

   417	  });

   193	  open-bundle (unsealed) limit death; the full seal→receive→relaunch happy
   194	  path.
   195	- **Model-level failover (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 4)**: the resolver
   196	  gains entry-level avoidance — `avoidEntries: [{platform, model}]` alongside
   197	  the existing platform-level `avoid[]` — and the classifier gains a
   198	  `model-unavailable` signature class (distinct from usage-limit; seeded with
   199	  the verified account-tier rejection string). A model rejected at spawn adds
   200	  its {platform, model} entry to avoidEntries and re-resolves: other models
   201	  on the SAME platform remain selectable. Named test: first chain entry
   202	  rejected as model-unavailable → the next entry on the same platform is
   203	  selected, with no platform-wide avoidance.
   204	  All platforms/entries exhausted → the loop parks with a resume-at hint
   205	  instead of dying.
   206	- **Caps**: every gate loops at most 5 iterations; on exhaustion the loop
   207	  parks and escalates (writes `.handoff/loop/ESCALATION.md`, notifies) — never
   208	  a 6th run.
   209	
   210	### `baton pipeline` (Layer 3 — a loop preset)
   211	
   212	- `baton pipeline run` = `loop run` with the dual-worktree subtask cycle:
   213	  - Two persistent worktrees `.worktrees/wt-a`, `.worktrees/wt-b`
   214	    (`git worktree add`); `pipeline init` ensure-lines `.worktrees/` into
   215	    `.gitignore` (same idempotent machinery as the `.handoff/` line).
   216	  - Subtask N: the writer seat implements on a namespaced branch
   217	    (`baton/wt-<seat>/subtask-N`) in its worktree; the reviewer seat reviews
   218	    the diff from the OTHER worktree (fresh checkout, fresh context). Seats
   219	    swap every subtask: worker-a writes / worker-b reviews → worker-b writes /
   220	    worker-a reviews → … (concrete models per seat come from the role
   221	    matrix — see Role-matrix additions).
   222	  - Verdict flow: APPROVED → the merger role adversarially re-checks and
   223	    merges into main (the ONLY writer to main); BLOCKED → writer fixes,
   224	    ≤5 iterations, then escalate. After each merge both worktrees
   225	    fast-forward.
   226	
   227	  **Worktree transaction layer (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 5)** —
   228	  `worktrees.mjs` treats every git operation as a guarded transaction:
   229	  - Branch namespace `baton/wt-*/…` is loop-owned; anything else is never
   230	    touched.
   231	  - Preflight before each child: worktree exists in `git worktree list`,
   232	    index clean, HEAD on the expected branch — a dirty or drifted worktree
   233	    parks the subtask instead of spawning.
   234	  - Postflight after each child: HEAD still on the expected branch, main
   235	    unmoved by the child — violation parks with the evidence.

   273	### Acceptance constraints (the loop's exit condition)
   274	
   275	1. On a fixture repo, `baton loop run` drives a toy goal end-to-end headlessly:
   276	   plan → gate-1 → smoke slice AS A TDD MINI-CYCLE (failing smoke assertion
   277	   authored and verifier-approved BEFORE the slice implementation — order
   278	   asserted from the journal) → parked for approval → (approved) → 2 subtasks
   279	   TDD → gate-2 → done, with review artifacts under `reviews/` in the fixture.
   280	   Layer-2 children run in the main root with live hooks and neither mutate
   281	   NOR read the supervisor-owned bundle: under `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1`,
   282	   hook commands on all three platforms produce zero bundle writes AND zero
   283	   session-start resume context (both asserted).
   284	2. Simulated limit death (child exits with a verbatim limit banner) mid-subtask
   285	   → the loop seals, remaps the role off the dead platform, resumes on the
   286	   other harness, and completes the subtask. Chained A→B→A tested. Separately:
   287	   a model-unavailable rejection at spawn selects the NEXT entry on the same
   288	   platform (no platform-wide avoidance).
   289	3. `baton pipeline run` completes 2 subtasks with alternating writer/reviewer
   290	   across the two worktrees; the attribution range scan passes for main AND
   291	   both worker branch ranges (child commits included) — sole author, zero AI
   292	   attribution; reviewer children run read-only.
   293	4. The 5-cap parks + escalates on every gate (unit-forced exhaustion test);
   294	   no gate ever runs a 6th iteration. Killing the supervisor (and its
   295	   launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
   296	   journal and continues or parks, with no orphaned children.
   297	5. Deleting `.handoff/` and `.worktrees/` leaves the fixture repo exactly as
   298	   a plain git repo (no residue outside gitignored trees).
   299	6. All existing 878 tests stay green; the new suite covers spec validation,
   300	   state-machine transitions (unit, injected io), child verdict parsing
   301	   (fixture transcripts), failover (fake children), and worktree discipline.
   302	
   303	### Top risks
   304	
   305	1. **Headless permission surfaces** — Claude Code children need permission
   306	   flags that stay inside the sandboxed repo; reviewers get read-only
   307	   allowlists. Mitigation: per-role allowlist table + spike task 0.
   308	2. **Verdict-parse drift** — models sometimes wrap the tail; the
   309	   region-bounded parser (Child supervision contract) takes the LAST tail in
   310	   the final-message region only and treats an unparseable one as
   311	   BLOCKED-with-escalation, never as APPROVED.
   312	3. **Cost runaway** — per-phase child caps + iteration caps + the smoke gate
   313	   before any full-run spend; every child's token/duration logged to the loop
   314	   journal.
   315	4. **Worktree state divergence** — only the merger writes main; workers are
   316	   branch-jailed; ff-sync after each merge; `baton pipeline doctor` checks
   317	   worktree health.
   318	5. **Cross-platform child API drift** — the spawn contract lives in ONE module
   319	   (children.mjs) with per-platform fixtures, same seam discipline as
   320	   normalize.mjs.

     1	/**
     2	 * Loop run state — snapshot + journal + replay for the Layer-2 supervisor,
     3	 * mirroring the bundle store's crash-tolerance idioms (atomic tmp+rename
     4	 * snapshots, torn-tail-tolerant NDJSON, seq-dedup replay). Everything lives
     5	 * under <root>/.handoff/loop/; the supervisor is the sole writer. Plan:
     6	 * docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md §"baton loop",
     7	 * §"Smoke gate", §"Supervisor lifetime and recovery", §"Caps".
